learnings.title: Ramp races
learnings.focus: Roll things down a propped-up book, guess which goes furthest, then change one thing and run it again.
getOut: A big hardback book and a cushion
A ball, a wooden block, an apple, a rolled-up sock
run: Prop the book on the cushion to make a ramp.
Send one thing at a time down it. Mark where each one stops.
Ask him to guess which goes furthest BEFORE each run.
Then change exactly one thing — steeper, or lay the towel over the ramp — and send the same thing again.
Compare: same object, one change, different result.
say: Which do you think goes furthest?
again: Race two things at once
Let him pick what to change
Guess before every single run

learnings.title: Pots & pans band
learnings.focus: Copy a beat, play it loud then soft, fast then slow, and swap the rhyming word in a song you both know.
getOut: A tub with rice in it
run: Round one — copy my beat. Two claps, then three, then long-short-long.
Round two — loud and soft, fast and slow, on command.
Round three — sing a whole song with the band playing, then swap the rhyming word: cat, hat, mat, sprat.
Put his hand flat on the pan straight after he hits it. It is still buzzing — that buzz IS the sound.
again: He leads and you copy
Add a third round he invents

learnings.title: Animal olympics
learnings.focus: Six animal-move stations called two at a time, finishing with throwing and catching.
getOut: A ball, for the last station
run: Set up six stations: frog jumps, flamingo stand, crab walk, kangaroo hops, bear crawl, throw and catch.
Call TWO at a time — "do the frog, then the flamingo" — so he has to hold both in mind.
Hold the flamingo to a count of five.
Count the catches out loud together.
say: Can you hold it to five?
again: He invents a station
Different order every round
Three instructions at a time

learnings.title: Treasure map
learnings.focus: Draw the house from above, mark an X, and send him to find the toy — then swap over.
run: Draw the house or garden FROM ABOVE — boxes for rooms, a squiggle for the sofa.
Say out loud that you are looking down from the sky, like a bird.
Mark an X where the toy is. He finds it.
Swap — he hides one and draws the map.
say: We're looking down from the sky
Is it left or right of the table?
Where are we on the map now?
again: Do it outside instead
Two X's on one map
He draws first

learnings.title: Toy shop
learnings.focus: His toys become stock, real coins change hands, and you swap roles halfway through.
run: He prices things 1p to 5p and writes the labels himself.
You buy. He counts out the change.
Ask for awkward things — more cars than blocks, fewer than three.
Swap roles halfway: you sell, he buys.
Sort the shop before opening — by size, by colour, by what it is made of.
say: Can I have fewer than three?
again: Sort the stock a different way each time
Give him a fixed amount to spend

learnings.title: His name in strange places
learnings.focus: His name written everywhere except paper — water on the patio, a finger through flour, chalk, a steamed-up window.
getOut: A paintbrush and a bucket of water
run: BIG first — whole arm, water on the patio.
Then smaller — a finger dragged through flour.
Then small — chalk on the path, or a bath crayon on a steamed-up window.
Never on paper. That is the whole point of it.
say: Big arm — all the way round
again: Write your names too
Just the first letter when he tires of it

learnings.title: Word hunt
learnings.focus: Take three words out of a book, stick them on the wall, then spend the rest of the week finding them — in the kitchen, the garden, on the way to the car.
getOut: Any book with describing words in it — a That's Not My… is perfect
Three scraps of paper and some tape
A basket or a bag for what he collects
run: Read the book properly first, for the story. Don't teach anything yet.
Read it again. This time stop on three words and only three — rough, soft, shiny. Say each one and let him touch the patch.
Write each word on a scrap and tape it somewhere he walks past — the fridge, the back door, the bottom stair.
Now hunt the house. One more thing for each word. He decides what counts, not you.
Tip the basket out and sort it into piles — everything rough here, everything smooth there. Two piles work better than five.
Leave the words up all week. Every time you meet one, say it out loud: that wall is rough, this towel is soft.
say: Find me something else that's rough
Is that one rough, or smooth?
Which pile does it go in?
That's our word from the book!
again: Three new words from a different book
He picks the words this time
Hunt outside only — bark, stones, leaves, the gate
Friday: take the scraps down and see if he still has them

learnings.title: Letter hunt
learnings.focus: Pick a letter, write it big on a card, then hunt it across everything in the cupboard that has writing on it — matching the shape in his hand to the shapes on the packets.
getOut: A blank card or a piece of paper, for the letter
Eight or so things from the cupboard that have writing on them — cereal boxes, tins, jars, a bottle, a bag of pasta
A pen, and sticky labels or masking tape
run: Pick the letter. Start with the one his name begins with — that's the one he cares about. Mummy's, daddy's and Millie's come another day.
He writes it big on the card. Help him if he needs it, but his hand holds the pen. That card is what he carries round.
Spread the packets on the floor, writing facing up. Every one has to have words on it — that's the whole game.
He holds his card up against a packet and looks for the same shape. Found one, the packet goes in a pile. He is matching a shape, not remembering a letter — the card does the remembering for him.
Ask where it is without letting him point. Above the picture, under the big word, on the side.
Say what each bit of print is FOR. The big word is its name. The little numbers say when to eat it by. The picture is not the words.
Finish by labelling three things that belong to whoever the letter is for — his drawer, his cup, his box — in his own handwriting.
say: Hold your card up next to it. Is it the same shape?
Where is it? Tell me without pointing.
Which bit is the name of it?
That's mummy's letter — what else has she got?
again: Mummy's letter, then daddy's, then Millie's
The bathroom shelf instead of the kitchen
A mark on paper for every one he finds, then count the marks
No card this time — see if he remembers the shape
